description.narrative:
Det övergripande målet för denna insats är att de mänskliga rättigheterna för alla ska skyddas och respekteras i Moçambique.
OHCHR organiserar sitt arbete för att uppnå detta mål i fem centrala insatsområden:
- Juridisk expertrådgivning, tekniskt bistånd och kapacitetsuppbyggnad för att stödja och stärka de nationella institutionernas efterlevnad av normer och standarder för mänskliga rättigheter samt engagemang i mekanismer för mänskliga rättigheter.
- Övervakning, analys och rapportering av utvecklingen av de mänskliga rättigheterna i syfte att få till stånd korrigerande åtgärder och ge beslutsunderlag till viktiga intressenter, inklusive nationella partner och FN-partner.
- Främja dialog och fungera som sammankallande för olika intressenter, inklusive det civila samhället och grupper i utsatta situationer, för att skapa utrymme för deras deltagande och engagemang i försvaret av deras rättigheter.
- Förespråka mänskliga rättigheter och öka medvetenheten för att främja förändringar i lagstiftning, beteenden och institutioner som är i linje med människorättsnormer och ger effektiva rättsmedel för offer.
- Samordning och integrering av mänskliga rättigheter i planering och programmering av utveckling, fredsbyggande och humanitära insatser samt i FN:s övergripande insatser.
Enligt OHCHR:s förändringsteori kombineras ovanstående centrala insatsområden för att uppnå tre huvudmål för hela OHCHR:s verksamhet i Moçambique: MÅL 1: Stärka rättsstatsprincipen och ansvarsutkrävande för brott mot de mänskliga rättigheterna.
MÅL 2: Öka deltagandet och skydda det medborgerliga utrymmet samt motverka diskriminering.
MÅL 3: Främja hållbar utveckling genom mänskliga rättigheter.

The overall objective of this intervention is that the human rights of all are protected and respected in Mozambique.
OHCHR organise their work to achieve this objective in five core intervention areas:
- Expert legal advice, technical assistance and capacity-building to support and strengthen compliance of national institutions with human rights norms and standards, and engagement with human rights mechanisms.
- Monitoring, analysis and reporting of human rights developments with the aim to seek corrective action and inform decision-making by key stakeholders, including national and UN partners.
- Facilitation of dialogue and acting as a convener of diverse stakeholders, including civil society and groups in situations of vulnerability, to create space for their participation and engagement in the defence of their rights.
- Human rights advocacy and awareness raising to promote changes in legislation, behaviours and institutions that are aligned with human rights standards and deliver effective remedies for victims.
- Coordination and mainstreaming of human rights in development, peacebuilding, and humanitarian planning, programming, and overall UN responses.
According to the OHCHR theory of change, the above core intervention areas combine to address three main goals for the entire OHCHR operations in Mozambique:
GOAL 1: Strengthen the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations.
GOAL 2: Enhance participation and protect civic space and counter discrimination.
GOAL 3: Advance sustainable development through human rights.

OHCHR organise their work to achieve this objective in five core intervention areas:
- Expert legal advice, technical assistance and capacity-building to support and strengthen compliance of national institutions with human rights norms and standards, and engagement with human rights mechanisms.
- Monitoring, analysis and reporting of human rights developments with the aim to seek corrective action and inform decision-making by key stakeholders, including national and UN partners.
- Facilitation of dialogue and acting as a convener of diverse stakeholders, including civil society and groups in situations of vulnerability, to create space for their participation and engagement in the defence of their rights.
- Human rights advocacy and awareness raising to promote changes in legislation, behaviours and institutions that are aligned with human rights standards and deliver effective remedies for victims.
- Coordination and mainstreaming of human rights in development, peacebuilding, and humanitarian planning, programming, and overall UN responses.
According to the OHCHR theory of change, the above core intervention areas combine to address three main goals for the entire OHCHR operations in Mozambique:
GOAL 1: Strengthen the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations.
GOAL 2: Enhance participation and protect civic space and counter discrimination.
GOAL 3: Advance sustainable development through human rights.
Brief summary of the planned interventions for each of the three goals:
GOAL 1: Strengthen the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations.
- Strengthening the capacity of justice actors to apply human rights standards in the administration of justice and provide accountability for human rights violations, by providing technical assistance and capacity-building to judges, prosecutors, and public defenders and facilitating dialogue amongst them to promote understanding and application of human rights standards in the administration of justice, particularly in situations of conflict and counterterrorism.
- Strengthening human rights compliance and the protection of civilians in conflict by security institutions, through capacity-building and technical assistance on human rights including the integration of modules in military academies and schools, the review of internal policies and procedures, and the set-up of oversight and accountability mechanisms for addressing human rights violations by these forces.
- Strengthening the mandate and capacities of the National Human Rights Commission, including a National Preventive Mechanism to bolster its role in promoting the implementation of human rights standards and recommendations of human rights mechanisms. This will be done through legal advice on the draft law regulating the Commission to align it with the Paris Principles, and technical assistance and capacity-building on monitoring and reporting and other functions relevant to its mandate.
- Building the capacity of the Inter-ministerial Commission on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law, through the provision of technical assistance and training to enhance its capabilities as well as advocacy to enhance the implementation of human rights recommendations and State compliance with its obligations.
GOAL 2: Enhance participation and protect civic space and counter discrimination.
- Strengthening the ability of civil society organisations and human rights defenders - including women and environmental defenders - to monitor, report and advocate for human rights, including through engagement with human rights mechanisms and participation in decision and policy-making processes, and by providing capacity-building and acting as a convener of diverse groups for the defence of their rights.
- Promoting the adoption and implementation of laws and policies that protect civic space and promote equality and counter discrimination, particularly those upholding the rights of persons with disabilities, by providing legal advice and other technical assistance to Parliament, Government, and other relevant stakeholders, and monitoring implementation and providing support for effective enforcement of relevant laws.
- Mainstreaming human rights and leave no one behind approaches in development, peacebuilding, and humanitarian responses. This entails supporting the UNCT to engage coherently to promote and protect civic space, including based on human rights monitoring and analysis of civic space trends, the situation of human rights defenders, and electoral processes, and through targeted advocacy drawing on evidence-based analysis.
GOAL 3: Advance sustainable development through human rights.
- Strengthening the capacity of national institutions to develop and implement a national action plan on business and human rights, and to review normative frameworks relevant to business operations for their compliance with human rights standards. This will be done through providing technical assistance and support to the Ministry of Justice and other institutions, and through contributing to analysis of key legislative and policy review processes related to business activities to identify gaps and recommend improvements.
- Engaging the private sector, through awareness raising, training and technical advice to companies, with a focus on the extractive sector, to develop and implement human rights policies and conduct human rights due diligence, as well as encouraging private sector participation in initiatives promoting human rights in business.
- Strengthening the capacity of national institutions to address claims appropriately and provide effective remedies for victims of business-related human rights abuses and environmental harms, through training and technical support, and monitoring developments in emblematic cases and advocating for corrective action.
- Raising awareness and strengthening the capacity of civil society actors to monitor and advocate for the protection of human rights in the context of business activities. This will be done mainly through training, joint monitoring missions and acting as a convener for diverse civil society actors to engage in dialogue and exchange of views, amongst them as well as with the private sector and national institutions.
